A sensor device is configured to operate in cooperation with a control device. The sensor device receives operating power from the control device through a power supply terminal and a ground terminal. The power supply terminal supplies a source voltage from the control device to the sensor device, while the ground terminal provides a reference potential shared between the sensor device and the control device.

The sensor device outputs a sensor signal to the control device in the form of a sensor output voltage. This sensor output voltage is transmitted from a sensor output terminal of the sensor device to the control device through a sensor output line. The control device detects the voltage on the sensor output line and determines a measured physical quantity based on the detected voltage.

The control device includes a constant voltage source and a pull-up resistor. The pull-up resistor is connected between the constant voltage source and the sensor output line. As a result, the sensor output line is pulled up toward a predetermined voltage when it is not being actively pulled down by the sensor device. This configuration allows the voltage on the sensor output line to be controlled in accordance with the operating state of the sensor device.

The sensor device includes a physical quantity detection unit configured to detect a physical quantity, such as pressure, temperature, position, acceleration, or another measurable parameter. The physical quantity detection unit changes or generates a voltage according to the detected physical quantity. This voltage serves as an internal detection signal representing the measured physical quantity.

To generate and control the sensor output voltage, the sensor device includes a regulator, an open-collector operational amplifier, and a plurality of resistor elements. The regulator generates a stable internal power supply voltage from the power supplied through the power supply terminal. The physical quantity detection unit operates using this regulated voltage and produces a voltage corresponding to the measured physical quantity.

The open-collector operational amplifier controls the voltage at the sensor output terminal based on the voltage generated by the physical quantity detection unit. Because the operational amplifier has an open-collector output, it can pull the sensor output line toward the ground potential but does not actively drive the line to a high voltage. Instead, the pull-up resistor in the control device raises the sensor output line toward the constant voltage source. The resistor elements in the sensor device are arranged to set reference voltages, adjust signal levels, and determine the relationship between the detected physical quantity and the resulting sensor output terminal voltage.

Accordingly, the sensor device and the control device together form a signal transmission system in which the sensor device receives power from the control device, detects a physical quantity, and outputs a corresponding sensor output voltage through the sensor output line. The voltage at the sensor output terminal is controlled by the cooperation of the pull-up resistor in the control device and the regulator, open-collector operational amplifier, and resistor elements in the sensor device.
outputs.L4:
A sensor device is provided that is configured to receive electric power from an external control device and to transmit a sensor output signal back to the control device. The sensor device includes a power-supply terminal connected to a power-supply line of the control device, a ground terminal connected to a ground line of the control device, and a sensor output terminal connected to an input terminal of the control device. Through these terminals, the sensor device can operate using power supplied by the control device while providing an output voltage representative of a detected physical quantity.

The sensor device includes a physical quantity detection unit that detects a predetermined physical quantity, such as pressure, temperature, acceleration, magnetic field strength, humidity, or another measurable environmental or operating condition. The physical quantity detection unit generates an electrical signal corresponding to the detected physical quantity. This signal may be a voltage, current, or other electrical characteristic that changes in accordance with the value of the physical quantity being measured.

A regulator is provided in the sensor device to generate a stable internal power-supply voltage from the power supplied by the control device. Since the voltage supplied from the control device may fluctuate due to wiring resistance, noise, load changes, or variations in the control device power source, the regulator stabilizes the voltage used by the internal circuitry of the sensor device. As a result, the physical quantity detection unit and related signal-processing components can operate reliably and produce an accurate detection signal.

The sensor device further includes an operational amplifier having an open-collector output configuration. The operational amplifier receives, directly or indirectly, a signal based on the output of the physical quantity detection unit. The open-collector output of the operational amplifier is connected to the sensor output terminal and is capable of pulling the voltage at the sensor output terminal toward the ground potential when activated. Because the open-collector configuration does not actively drive the output terminal to a high level, the high-level voltage of the sensor output terminal can be determined by an external or internal pull-up structure, such as a resistor network connected to the power-supply side.

Voltage-divider resistors are also provided to define or adjust the voltage applied to the sensor output terminal. These resistors may be arranged between the power-supply terminal, the ground terminal, and the sensor output terminal so that a desired reference voltage or output voltage range is established. By selecting appropriate resistance values, the voltage level at the sensor output terminal can be controlled to fall within an input voltage range suitable for the control device. This allows the control device to accurately recognize the sensor output without being exposed to an excessive voltage or an unstable signal.

In operation, power and ground are supplied from the control device to the sensor device. The regulator generates a stable internal voltage, and the physical quantity detection unit detects the target physical quantity and produces a corresponding detection signal. The operational amplifier controls the state of the open-collector output in accordance with the detection signal. When the operational amplifier output transistor is turned on, current flows through the voltage-divider or pull-up path and the voltage at the sensor output terminal is lowered. When the operational amplifier output transistor is turned off, the sensor output terminal is raised to a voltage determined by the resistor network. In this manner, the output terminal voltage is controlled in accordance with the physical quantity detected by the physical quantity detection unit.

This configuration enables the sensor output terminal voltage to be appropriately controlled even when the sensor device is powered by the control device. Since the output voltage is set using the open-collector operational amplifier and the voltage-divider resistors, the sensor device can provide a signal that is compatible with the input specifications of the control device. The control device can therefore receive the sensor output reliably and determine the measured physical quantity based on the voltage supplied from the sensor output terminal.

The described arrangement is advantageous because it allows the sensor device to maintain stable internal operation while also ensuring that the transmitted output voltage is properly regulated or limited. This improves measurement reliability, reduces the influence of supply-voltage fluctuation, and helps prevent erroneous detection by the control device. Accordingly, the sensor device is suitable for applications requiring dependable detection and transmission of physical quantity information, such as automotive systems, industrial control systems, environmental monitoring devices, and other electronic control applications.
outputs.L5:
In electronics, the terms **Vcc**, **Gnd**, and **Vout** are commonly used to describe important points in a circuit.

**Vcc** usually refers to the positive supply voltage of a circuit. It is the voltage that powers components such as microcontrollers, sensors, logic gates, and integrated circuits. For example, in a 5V circuit, Vcc may be connected to +5 volts, while in a 3.3V circuit it may be connected to +3.3 volts.

**Gnd**, or ground, is the reference point for the circuit. It is often considered 0 volts and serves as the common return path for electric current. All voltage measurements in a circuit are usually made relative to Gnd. For a circuit to work correctly, all connected components typically need to share a common ground.

**Vout** means output voltage. It is the voltage produced by a circuit, sensor, amplifier, voltage regulator, or other electronic device. For example, a temperature sensor may receive power from Vcc and Gnd, then provide a changing Vout signal that represents the measured temperature.

Together, **Vcc**, **Gnd**, and **Vout** are often found on electronic modules and sensors. A typical connection would be: Vcc to the power supply, Gnd to ground, and Vout to the input of another circuit or a microcontroller. Understanding these three labels is essential for building and troubleshooting electronic circuits.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style description of an embodiment of a sensor device connected to a control device, including terminals, power/ground/output lines, a constant voltage source, pull-up resistor, detection unit, regulator, open-collector op amp, and voltage divider resistors.
counterfactuals.output:
In one embodiment, a sensor system includes a sensor device electrically connected to a control device through a plurality of terminals and corresponding signal lines. The control device may be, for example, an electronic control unit, a controller, or another processing device configured to supply electric power to the sensor device and to receive an output signal therefrom.

The control device includes a power terminal, a ground terminal, and an output-signal input terminal. The power terminal is connected to a power line for supplying electric power to the sensor device, the ground terminal is connected to a ground line defining a reference potential, and the output-signal input terminal is connected to an output line for receiving a detection signal from the sensor device.

The control device further includes a constant voltage source configured to generate a predetermined supply voltage. The constant voltage source is connected to the power line so as to supply operating power to the sensor device. A pull-up resistor is connected between the constant voltage source, or a voltage derived therefrom, and the output line. Accordingly, when the output line is not actively pulled toward ground by the sensor device, the output line is biased to a high-level voltage through the pull-up resistor.

A detection unit is connected to the output line in the control device. The detection unit is configured to detect a voltage level of the output line and to determine a state of the sensor device based on the detected voltage level. For example, the detection unit may distinguish between a high-level state, a low-level state, and, in some embodiments, an abnormal state such as an open circuit or short circuit.

The sensor device includes a power terminal connected to the power line, a ground terminal connected to the ground line, and an output terminal connected to the output line. The sensor device further includes a regulator connected between the power terminal and internal circuitry of the sensor device. The regulator is configured to generate a regulated internal voltage from the voltage supplied through the power line. The regulated internal voltage may be used as an operating voltage for a sensing element, signal processing circuitry, or comparison circuitry included in the sensor device.

The sensor device also includes an operational amplifier configured as an open-collector output circuit. The open-collector output of the operational amplifier is connected to the output terminal of the sensor device. The operational amplifier is configured such that, when a predetermined detection condition is satisfied, the open-collector output is turned on to draw current from the output line to the ground line, thereby producing a low-level output signal at the output-signal input terminal of the control device. Conversely, when the predetermined detection condition is not satisfied, the open-collector output is turned off, and the output line is pulled up through the pull-up resistor of the control device to produce a high-level output signal.

In the sensor device, a voltage divider circuit is provided by a first resistor and a second resistor connected in series between a predetermined voltage node and the ground line. A divided voltage generated at a connection node between the first resistor and the second resistor is supplied to an input terminal of the operational amplifier. The predetermined voltage node may be connected to the regulated internal voltage generated by the regulator, to the power line, or to a signal generated by a sensing element. The voltage divider circuit thereby provides a reference voltage or a detection voltage used by the operational amplifier to determine whether the output line should be pulled low.

In a particular configuration, the operational amplifier includes a first input terminal receiving a sensor signal corresponding to a physical quantity detected by a sensing element and a second input terminal receiving the divided voltage generated by the first and second voltage divider resistors. The operational amplifier compares the sensor signal with the divided voltage. When the sensor signal exceeds, or falls below, the divided voltage depending on the polarity of the circuit, the operational amplifier changes the state of the open-collector output. As a result, the voltage level appearing on the output line represents the detection state of the sensor device.

Because the pull-up resistor is arranged in the control device and the output stage of the sensor device is formed as an open-collector circuit, the sensor device can transmit a detection result to the control device using a simple output line while allowing the output voltage level to be determined by the control device. This configuration also permits the control device to monitor the output line for fault conditions and enables stable signal transmission even when the sensor device and the control device are connected by a harness or cable.

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a formal patent specification excerpt for a sensor device where power is supplied via Vcc/Gnd, output is sent via Vout, and the device includes a physical quantity detection unit, regulator, open-collector operational amplifier, and voltage divider.
counterfactuals.output:
## Patent Specification Excerpt

### Title  
**Sensor Device Having Regulated Power Supply and Open-Collector Output Conditioning Circuit**

### Technical Field  
The present disclosure relates generally to sensor devices and, more particularly, to a sensor device configured to receive operating power through supply terminals, detect a physical quantity, condition a detection signal using an operational amplifier having an open-collector output stage, and provide an output signal through an output terminal.

### Background  
Sensor devices are commonly used to detect physical quantities such as pressure, temperature, magnetic field, acceleration, displacement, humidity, or light intensity. Such devices often require a stable internal operating voltage and an output circuit capable of interfacing with external control circuitry. In certain applications, it is desirable to provide a compact sensor device having a limited number of terminals, for example a power supply terminal, a ground terminal, and an output terminal, while still ensuring stable operation and reliable signal transmission.

### Summary  
According to one aspect, a sensor device includes a power supply terminal configured to receive a supply voltage, a ground terminal, and an output terminal configured to output a detection signal. The sensor device further includes a physical quantity detection unit configured to generate a sensor signal corresponding to a detected physical quantity, a regulator configured to generate a regulated internal voltage from the supply voltage supplied between the power supply terminal and the ground terminal, an operational amplifier having an open-collector output, and a voltage divider connected to the operational amplifier. The operational amplifier is configured to receive a signal based on the sensor signal and to generate an amplified or conditioned signal at the open-collector output. The voltage divider is configured to define at least one reference or bias voltage used by the operational amplifier and/or to condition the output signal supplied to the output terminal.

### Brief Description of the Drawings  
**FIG. 1** is a schematic block diagram of a sensor device according to an embodiment.  
**FIG. 2** is an exemplary circuit diagram illustrating a regulator, a physical quantity detection unit, an open-collector operational amplifier, and a voltage divider coupled to an output terminal.

### Detailed Description  

Referring to FIG. 1, a sensor device 10 includes a power supply terminal **Vcc**, a ground terminal **Gnd**, and an output terminal **Vout**. The power supply terminal Vcc is configured to receive an external supply voltage from an external power source, and the ground terminal Gnd is configured to be connected to a reference potential. The output terminal Vout is configured to transmit an electrical output signal representing a physical quantity detected by the sensor device 10.

The sensor device 10 includes a physical quantity detection unit 20. The physical quantity detection unit 20 may include, for example, a pressure-sensitive element, a thermosensitive element, a Hall element, a magnetoresistive element, a capacitive detection element, a piezoelectric detection element, a photodetector, or another transducer suitable for generating an electrical sensor signal in response to a physical quantity. The physical quantity detection unit 20 outputs a detection signal corresponding to the magnitude, presence, or variation of the physical quantity.

A regulator 30 is coupled between the power supply terminal Vcc and the ground terminal Gnd. The regulator 30 is configured to generate a regulated internal supply voltage for one or more internal circuits of the sensor device 10, including the physical quantity detection unit 20 and/or signal processing circuitry. By supplying a regulated voltage, the regulator 30 reduces variation in the output signal due to fluctuation of the external supply voltage applied to Vcc.

The sensor device 10 further includes an operational amplifier 40 having an open-collector output stage. An input of the operational amplifier 40 is coupled directly or indirectly to the physical quantity detection unit 20 so as to receive a signal based on the detected physical quantity. The operational amplifier 40 may function as an amplifier, comparator, buffer, threshold detector, or signal-conditioning circuit. The open-collector output stage permits the output node to be pulled to a low potential by the operational amplifier 40 while allowing an external or internal pull-up element to define a high-level output state.

A voltage divider 50 is provided in the sensor device 10. The voltage divider 50 may include a first resistor and a second resistor connected in series between the regulated internal voltage and the ground terminal Gnd, or between the power supply terminal Vcc and the ground terminal Gnd. A divided voltage generated at an intermediate node of the voltage divider 50 may be supplied to one input of the operational amplifier 40 as a reference voltage. In one embodiment, the operational amplifier 40 compares the sensor signal from the physical quantity detection unit 20 with the reference voltage produced by the voltage divider 50, and drives the open-collector output according to the comparison result.

The output terminal Vout is coupled to the open-collector output of the operational amplifier 40. In one embodiment, a pull-up resistor is connected between Vout and Vcc, either within the sensor device 10 or externally to the sensor device 10. When the operational amplifier 40 turns on its open-collector output transistor, the output terminal Vout is pulled toward the ground potential. When the open-collector output transistor is turned off, the output terminal Vout is pulled toward a high-level voltage by the pull-up resistor. Accordingly, the sensor device 10 may provide a digital or threshold-based output signal corresponding to the physical quantity detected by the physical quantity detection unit 20.

In another embodiment, the voltage divider 50 may be connected to the output terminal Vout so as to scale, bias, or otherwise define the output voltage supplied through Vout. The voltage divider 50 may also be used to set hysteresis, offset, or a switching threshold for the operational amplifier 40. Additional resistive, capacitive, or protective elements may be provided to stabilize the circuit, suppress noise, or protect the terminals Vcc, Gnd, and Vout from electrostatic discharge or overvoltage conditions.

In operation, electrical power is supplied to the sensor device 10 through Vcc and Gnd. The regulator 30 produces a stable internal voltage, and the physical quantity detection unit 20 generates a sensor signal in accordance with a detected physical quantity. The operational amplifier 40 processes the sensor signal with reference to a voltage established by the voltage divider 50. The open-collector output of the operational amplifier 40 then controls the electrical state of the output terminal Vout, thereby allowing an external circuit to receive the detection result.

### Exemplary Claim  

1. A sensor device comprising:  
   a power supply terminal configured to receive a supply voltage;  
   a ground terminal;  
   an output terminal configured to output a detection signal;  
   a physical quantity detection unit configured to generate a sensor signal corresponding to a detected physical quantity;  
   a regulator coupled to the power supply terminal and configured to generate a regulated internal voltage;  
   an operational amplifier having an open-collector output coupled to the output terminal, the operational amplifier being configured to receive a signal based on the sensor signal; and  
   a voltage divider configured to generate a divided voltage supplied to the operational amplifier as a reference or bias voltage,  
   wherein the operational amplifier controls a voltage level at the output terminal according to the sensor signal and the divided voltage.

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe the architecture of a sensor device connected to an ECU/control device, with terminals 7–9, constant voltage source 11, pull-up resistor 12, and internal components 2–6, in patent application language.
counterfactuals.output:
In one embodiment, a sensor device is connected to an electronic control unit (ECU) or control device via a plurality of connection terminals. The sensor device includes internal circuit components 2 to 6, which are accommodated in a sensor housing and electrically connected to external terminals 7, 8, and 9. The terminals 7 to 9 provide an electrical interface between the sensor device and the control device.

The control device includes a constant voltage source 11 and a pull-up resistor 12. The constant voltage source 11 supplies a predetermined regulated voltage to the sensor device through one of the terminals, for example terminal 7. Another terminal, for example terminal 9, is connected to a reference potential such as ground. A signal terminal, for example terminal 8, is connected to an output node of the sensor device and to the pull-up resistor 12 provided in the control device. The pull-up resistor 12 is connected between the signal terminal and the constant voltage source 11, thereby biasing the signal line to a predetermined voltage level when the output of the sensor device is in a high-impedance state or is not actively driven.

The internal components 2 to 6 of the sensor device may include a sensing element, a signal processing circuit, a switching element, a protection circuit, and/or a diagnostic circuit. The sensing element detects a physical quantity, such as position, pressure, temperature, speed, or magnetic field. The signal processing circuit processes an output of the sensing element and generates a corresponding electrical signal. The switching element may selectively pull the signal terminal toward the reference potential in accordance with the processed sensor signal. As a result, the control device can detect a change in the voltage at the signal terminal and determine a state or measured value of the detected physical quantity.

In this configuration, the constant voltage source 11 provided in the control device supplies operating power and/or a bias voltage to the sensor device, while the pull-up resistor 12 establishes a defined signal level on the signal line. The sensor device can therefore transmit a detection signal to the control device using a simple terminal arrangement including the power supply terminal 7, the signal terminal 8, and the ground terminal 9. The control device monitors the voltage appearing at the signal terminal and performs control processing based on the monitored voltage.

Accordingly, the sensor device and the control device form a sensor system in which the sensor device is externally connected to the control device through the terminals 7 to 9, and in which the control device-side constant voltage source 11 and pull-up resistor 12 cooperate with the internal components 2 to 6 of the sensor device to generate a stable and reliably detectable sensor output signal.

The control device is configured to supply operating power to the sensor via the power line and to provide a pull-up function on the output signal line, for example by coupling the output signal line to a supply potential through a pull-up resistor. In operation, the operational amplifier compares a signal associated with the detection unit with a voltage established by the resistor divider and selectively sinks current from the output signal line through the open-collector output, while the pull-up function of the control device biases the output signal line to a predetermined logic level when the open-collector output is not conducting.
